hero.title: Is It OCD or Just a Habit?
hero.subtitle: Same action. Different experience.

stage_2.question: What happens next?
stage_2.quote_again: “I checked… but what if I missed something?”
stage_2.aha_sub: The action itself doesn't tell the whole story.
stage_2.aha_detail: Notice what happens around it: the doubt, the urge to respond, the temporary relief, and whether the doubt returns.

stage_3.headline: Both started with the same action.
stage_3.feedback_doubt: Notice how uncertainty enters the second experience.
stage_3.feedback_repetition: Notice how the same action happens again.
stage_3.feedback_relief: Notice how relief appears after responding.

stage_4.section_kicker: NOW TRY IT ON SOMETHING ELSE
stage_4.headline: Look beyond the action.

scenario_1.story: “I reread my message once before sending it. It looks good, so I send it.”
scenario_1.question: What stands out?
scenario_1.feedback_clear_stop: The action has a clear stopping point. Attention is able to move on.
scenario_1.feedback_repeated_doubt: Notice when looking once settles the question versus when doubt pulls back.
scenario_1.feedback_repeating_action: In this case, once checked, the action didn't need to be repeated.

scenario_2.story: “I turn the stove off. I look once. The burner is off. I leave.”
scenario_2.question: What stands out?
scenario_2.feedback_clear_stop: Looking once and moving on gives a natural sense of completion.
scenario_2.feedback_repeated_doubt: Notice whether doubt returns or whether seeing it off was enough.
scenario_2.feedback_need_recheck: Here, seeing the burner off settled the thought without returning.

stage_5.headline: When an action keeps pulling your attention back, notice:
stage_5.prompt_question: “What is making me question it again?”
stage_5.detail: An action can look ordinary from the outside. The experience around it can tell you more.
